Why the 2026 Sitting is Rated 8.6 Effort

The mathematical reality of the new 70+ cutoff threshold

In the 2011–2022 Cambridge era, candidates could achieve admission with composite scores between 42.5 and 52.8 points (~55% accuracy). At that threshold, aggressive guessing or skipping whole sub-sections (e.g., Physics) was a viable tactical compromise.

With the 2026 admission cutoff climbing to 70.1 points (Milan/Bologna 74+), a candidate must score net +70.1 out of 90. Under the IMAT scoring formula (+1.5 correct, −0.4 incorrect):

  • Candidate must answer at least 48 to 51 questions accurately.
  • Tolerates a maximum of 3 to 4 errors across the entire 60 questions.
  • Every single incorrect guess wastes 1.9 points against a correct answer (opportunity cost).
🎯

Discipline Volatility & Subject Priority Order

Ranked by variance and tactical ROI per hour of study

1. Biology (23 Questions • 34.5 pts) Top ROI

Represents 38.3% of the entire paper. Must achieve 21+ correct out of 23. Zero unforced errors tolerated in cytology and genetics.

2. Chemistry (15 Questions • 22.5 pts) Highest Volatility

Highest trap density. Master Le Chatelier, pH titrations, and organic functional groups to secure 12+ correct answers.

3. Physics & Math (13 Questions • 19.5 pts) The 70+ Decider

Historically neglected by candidates. In the 70+ era, you cannot leave these blank; you need at least 9–10 correct to surpass 70 points.
